What is here
- index.html, wp.js: the Wallpaper Engine edition (wallpaper/ in the upstream repository), unmodified, copied
  from commit 02174503d0f391b1bb2537b8cad75e8e5f9997f2.
- optics.html: a MODIFIED copy of index.html for this workbench. It keeps the original copyright notice and adds a
  modification notice. Changes: optics vocabulary for the ring labels and the callout (physical laws such as the
  thin-lens equation, never invented measurements), the random "METHODS" counter replaced by the run status the
  panel sends, decorative numbers beside optics keys replaced by words or by the run's own design values, and a
  small window.OPTICS bridge (setStatus, setVocab, setChecks, setTempo, pulse) the panel calls.
- LICENSE: the upstream license file, unmodified.
- Not included: wallpaper/audio/sw421k.mp3 (CC0 music, not covered by the license above). The panel turns the
  music off, so the request for that file returns 404 and nothing plays.

How the workbench uses it
- optics_graph/server.py serves /haloflux/ (optics.html), /haloflux/upstream.html (the unmodified original),
  wp.js and LICENSE, and nothing else.
- optics_graph/panel.html fades the animation in as a full-window overlay while the selected run is working,
  fades it out when the run stops working, and pauses it while hidden. The overlay credits "modified from
  HALOFLUX by Ryder191 (RYDER CODE / Ms MAIKEBAIs CAT)" with a link to the repository.
- The panel sets the upstream wallpaper properties at runtime (music off, side panels off) and feeds only real
  run data through window.OPTICS: status, the design's component ids, parameters and target x positions, test
  expressions, requirements and the decision being made. Bursts mark a node passing, flares a reroute.
- The animation is decorative. Nothing in it is an optical measurement or hardware motion.
